headline: The four-week build tops out with strain and tolerance level, leaving the base durable rather than overreached a month from the crossing.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your recent block has closed out a genuine volume build without the fatigue markers you'd expect if you'd overreached — strain and tolerance are sitting essentially level, which tells you the added load has been absorbed rather than accumulated as debt. That's the right place to be with the crossing inside a month: capacity is up, and the body isn't behind on it.

The most useful signal continues to be aerobic efficiency. Comparable-effort easy runs are averaging lower HR than the prior period, and yesterday's long run into today's brisker follow-up produced no HR drift — back-to-back durability is holding at higher pace, not just easy pace. Strength frequency has more than doubled over the block too, so the base you're carrying into St. Olavsleden is broad rather than purely mileage-driven.

Nothing here suggests the need to push harder from this peak. The build has done its job; the question now is how you consolidate it into event-specific readiness rather than chasing more raw volume.
watch_items: Whether pack-loaded running enters the schedule now that the crossing is inside a month — the base is there, but the specific demand isn't yet trained.
Whether per-run climbing starts building toward sustained ascent rather than the rolling profiles seen so far.
Whether the strain:tolerance balance stays level or tips if volume is held here versus pushed further.
Whether short-sleep nights start clustering as longer efforts continue, given the wide night-to-night swing lately.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 190 km vs 126 km prior block (+51%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 145 bpm vs 153 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 8 runs)
▬ Strain:tolerance ratio 0.99 (MAINTAINING) (strain 91, tolerance 92); sleep averaging 7h29m over the same period
